Izzarak: But what brings Motua here?
DM: I am weak these days.
DM: The whirlwind drains my power.
Kenzo: What is the cause of the whirlwind?
Izzarak: It's Motua that he says—who are—well, what is Motua doing, you know? Not—
DM: On a rampage. Wounded, angry, lost, trapped!
DM: I do not care what to. It must be slaughtered, driven out.
DM: You just point in you—like, reaches up and sort of gestures towards you. You're not listening, human.
DM: Motua, from beyond—from the veil came here to destroy us or something. He drained my energy away.
Izzarak: Am I aware of anything in the direction or location that they are referring to?
DM: Ah, like, what do you mean?
Izzarak: Can I see something there?

DM: It's a pretty thick jungle, right? So like you could see, you know, maybe a hundred feet. There's—I mean they're talking like miles away, you could, you know, climb up to the top of the volcano. You might get a better view, although it might be dangerous.
Izzarak: But it's not at the location of our humanoid immortal?
DM: No, no, no, it's not, it's. It's like towards the center of the footprint of the gods.
DM: So like the volcano is sort of north of here, and this is talking West.
DM: Well, something must be done.
Kenzo: So I'm using where to go there. Can we speak with Motua?
Kenzo: What form does Motua—what form? Yes.
Kenzo: If we cause Motua to calm down or return home, then will you be able to stop this?
DM: Once, all of fire was mine to command. I could—he reaches his hand, and sort of.
DM: I could push this way, I could conduct it like a symphony. I could control the flames.
DM: Now Motua has destroyed it all.
Kenzo: What is your name, friend?
DM: You may call me Ember.

Kenzo: Well, my name is Kenzo, and my friends and I here— We will do our best to tame Motua, or at least render its— turbulence, so that— you may do that— regain your powers and tame this fire once more.
DM: That would be most welcome.
Kenzo: What can you tell us of Motua? What advice can you give us to help increase the odds that we succeed in our quest?
DM: I have not dared, not with my—
DM: Do you not feel the pull? Feel it dragging at your soul?
Kenzo: I do. But what can we do to prepare?
Izzarak: What advice do you have for us?
DM: My advice? I wish I could tell you. If I knew what to do, I would have done it myself.
DM: I don't know if you can sneak up on such a creature, but—
Kenzo: Is fighting it the only way? Is there another way to subdue it or convince it to go home?
DM: It's destroyed my home. I would have it killed. I will not quarrel if that is not your way. But—
Kenzo: And is that a thing we can reason with? Where is its home? Can we trap it somehow?
DM: Its home, as I said, is the land of the dead. Cannot go to this.
Kenzo: Is there a way to send it back to return it there, from whence it came?
DM: There are many things that I can do, the power, the spirit realms, but I cannot reach the veil.
DM: I am bound to this place, this world.
DM: You, though, who can say?
DM: Flickering, ever changeable souls of such creatures as humans?
DM: Maybe you could lead the way. Maybe it would consume you and follow you to death.
Kenzo: Ah, I've already traversed that once. Huh! Perhaps I could again.

interactions.title: A local alliance and a blessing for the staff
lines: Kenzo: So, Ember, if we're successful in our quest, my hope is that we could be allies, and perhaps call upon you in the event we need your aid in the future.
DM: If you need my aid here, I would listen.

Kenzo: There's one thing I've learned about this land: sometimes travel is something that occurs against your will. I don't know how I ended up here six thousand miles from my own home, but it happened, so never say never, my friend.
DM: And here I thought that staff you hold was from these very woods.
Kenzo: It's from the elven woods thousands of miles from here.
DM: The energy of this place runs through it.
Kenzo: The staff has uh grown accustomed to the land here. It likes it here. I like it here, but I hope that our fellowship can extend beyond this moment.
DM: He holds up a finger, and it starts it like smokes and flames slightly, reaches out towards your staff. May I?
DM: He touches it, and he like traces a design of a rune that looks kind of like a ah one of these Ohana trees, and he, like flicks, and like red fire, runs through it.
DM: Perhaps that will be a blessing for you should you need it in the future.
Kenzo: Kenzo looks at the rune. What does it mean? What does it do?
DM: I have little power left, but—controls.
DM: It will fill with the energy of life and death of Ohana, of the—not just the—
DM: Somi-nai, the volcano. My home is life and death, fertility and destruction, speed, agonizing slowness all at once.
DM: Although there is very little power in this, can speed you up or slow down your enemies should you need it.
Kenzo: Ember, thank you, my friend. We will uh use this power wisely, and again when we return— I appreciate you for helping to bring balance back to this land as well.
DM: Sort of gives a bow and dives into the lava, and then begins swimming upriver back towards the volcano.

Kenzo: Doesn't seem like Ember's got much else to say in terms of like how they can help us with Motua.
Kenzo: But, um! I am interested in ways that we can stay in touch and be friends, because it's always valuable to have a fire spirit in your back pocket.
after: Kenzo: Sweet.
DM: And I think that is a good place to stop.
Izzarak: That's right.
DM: We will deal with how you will cross the Lava River tomorrow—next time.
